source.title: Agent Behavioral Contracts II: Certifying Compositional Reliability Without Assuming Independence

assessments.primary_source_quality: Very strong for a preprint: preregistered confirmatory design, deterministic gold scoring with no LLM judge, large sample, explicit null result, negative control, formal confidence intervals, and released contracts/scoring/analysis/preregistration. It is still a recent preprint and no independent external replication was located in this pass.
assessments.quantitative_result: In 18,000 preregistered two-agent handoff missions, same-model instances co-failed on 90.0% of missions where either failed; log OR 6.66 with 95% CI [6.38, 7.00], phi 0.916. Same-model marginal failure rates were about 39.4% and 37.2%, independence predicted roughly 14.6% co-failure while observed co-failure was 36.3%. Substituting a different model reduced association in six of six contrasts; substituting vendor after model identity already differed did not produce the preregistered ordering. A same-model negative-control pair returned null arm contrasts across the reported controls.
assessments.matched_baseline: Strong. The core hypothesis directly compares same-model versus different-model pair conditions across multiple topologies with preregistration and an unmanipulated negative-control pair. Independent mission draws rather than paired identical missions and capability differences between substituted models are important residual limitations.
assessments.ablation_or_causal_support: Strong for the tested proposition that model identity can create large failure dependence and that model substitution can reduce association in these contract tasks. The experiment is not a direct scientist-agent/research-review study, so transfer of magnitude is not established.
assessments.reproducibility_or_artifacts: Strong: contracts, deterministic scoring code, analysis scripts and preregistration are reported released.
assessments.external_replication: No independent replication located. Robustness across topologies/contrasts and preregistered null/negative controls provide substantial within-study robustness.
assessments.failure_evidence: Directly demonstrates that multiplying marginal reliabilities under independence can drastically over-credit redundancy when same-model components share error modes.
scope_limits: Retail/financial behavioral-contract tasks, not open-ended research synthesis or O.
Substituted models differ in capability, so model identity is not isolated from competence in all contrasts.
Do not transfer the 90% co-failure magnitude to other agent systems without matched measurement.

original_method_vs_o_adaptation.original_method_evidence: A- for measuring dependence before composing reliability claims in the tested task family and for rejecting naive same-model independence assumptions there.
original_method_vs_o_adaptation.o_specific_adaptation: Untested for O. O should measure matched item-level co-failure/complementarity before counting additional evaluators or agents as independent evidence; literature alone cannot set O's effective independence.

source.title: Nine Judges, Two Effective Votes: Correlated Errors Undermine LLM Evaluation Panels

assessments.primary_source_quality: Strong primary empirical study with item-level human/deterministic ground truth, nine frontier judges from seven model families, multiple datasets, robustness across prompts/temperatures/CoT, and a preference benchmark. Peer-review status and independent replication were not established in this pass.
assessments.quantitative_result: The paper reports that nine judges provide only about two effective independent votes. The worker record gives MNLI n_eff=2.18 [2.07, 2.31], panel accuracy 72.0% versus best individual 71.8%, while an independence-calibrated Condorcet model predicts roughly 94%, producing about a 22-point gap. Replications include SNLI, AlphaNLI and RewardBench with similarly low effective independence; the paper abstract states actual panel accuracy falls 8-22 points short of the independent-voting ideal and established aggregation methods close at most 11% of the gap.
assessments.matched_baseline: Strong for the central claim: actual correlated panel performance is compared against the same judges' independence-calibrated null and against best individual judges on identical items. It is not a randomized intervention that creates independence, but the measurement target is dependence rather than a treatment effect.
assessments.ablation_or_causal_support: Strong for the measurement claim that raw panel size overstates independent information in the tested evaluation tasks. Weaker for any specific remedy beyond directly selecting empirically complementary evaluators.
assessments.reproducibility_or_artifacts: The paper reports detailed datasets/estimators and robustness analyses; this pass did not independently run released code.
assessments.external_replication: No direct independent replication located. Cross-dataset, prompt, temperature, CoT and RewardBench robustness is substantial equivalent within-study robustness.
assessments.failure_evidence: Strong: best single judge matches or beats the full panel across conditions, and smarter aggregation does not recover most of the independence gap.
scope_limits: NLI and preference evaluation are not autonomous scientific review.
Family/vendor labels are poor proxies for complementarity in this study, but that does not prove labels are never useful.
Effective sample size values are panel/task-specific and cannot be copied to O.

original_method_vs_o_adaptation.original_method_evidence: A- for using item-level error dependence/effective independence rather than nominal judge count in the studied evaluation panels.
original_method_vs_o_adaptation.o_specific_adaptation: Requires O-specific held-out items with external/mechanical truth to estimate covariance/effective votes. Separate calls, prompts or model-family labels cannot be assumed independent.

source.title: Diversity Collapse in Multi-Agent LLM Systems: Structural Coupling and Collective Failure in Open-Ended Idea Generation

assessments.primary_source_quality: Strong venue/provenance and broad empirical sweep. The study reports more than 10,000 proposals, metric sensitivity checks, human validation of diversity metrics, and released code/caches. The central endpoint is semantic diversity rather than downstream scientific correctness or implemented research success.
assessments.quantitative_result: The peer-reviewed paper reports Horizontal junior-dominated collaboration Vendi about 8.08 versus Interdisciplinary about 4.65, while overall quality ranges only 7.88-8.50. Group-size scaling raises absolute diversity but Vendi/N falls from 1.03 at N=3 to 0.47 at N=7. Metric sensitivity across OpenAI/BGE embeddings preserves the main ordering. The worker also records heterogeneous-model diversity gains, but those are diversity endpoints and some comparisons use limited topic counts.
assessments.matched_baseline: Moderate. Cognitive structures and group sizes are systematically compared across topics and repeated runs. Persona/authority structure changes multiple social/context variables at once, so 'independence before deliberation' is a synthesis over several manipulations rather than one isolated binary ablation.
assessments.ablation_or_causal_support: Moderate for the claim that interaction structure and group size materially affect semantic diversity. Weak-to-moderate for the broader claim that independent-first search improves downstream research value; the paper does not execute proposals or measure scientific correctness.
assessments.reproducibility_or_artifacts: Strong: ACL paper plus public code, embedding caches, LLM-as-judge evaluation caches and aggregated metrics.
assessments.failure_evidence: Strong for diversity saturation and structural convergence; not evidence that consensus structures are inferior on all downstream objectives.
scope_limits: Open-ended proposal ideation only; no implementation/execution endpoint.
Diversity is not equivalent to novelty correctness, scientific merit, or progress toward AGI.
Authority/persona manipulations can change style and verbosity as well as independence.
Heterogeneous-model results demonstrate semantic exploration changes, not automatically better decisions.

original_method_vs_o_adaptation.original_method_evidence: B for preserving ideation diversity through less structurally coupled interaction; C+ for claiming downstream research-quality improvement. Overall candidate graded B-.
original_method_vs_o_adaptation.o_specific_adaptation: Keeping exploration workers isolated before integration is plausible and evidence-aligned for diversity, but O-facing value must be measured by marginal unique evidence/decision improvement rather than semantic diversity alone.

cross_source_synthesis: Two independent primary studies strongly reject nominal redundancy as a substitute for measured independence: one through preregistered deterministic co-failure experiments, the other through item-level evaluator error correlations across multiple benchmarks.

The peer-reviewed diversity study supports isolation/structural decoupling as a way to preserve exploration breadth, but this is not itself evidence that more diverse research trajectories produce better scientific outcomes.

For O-specific use, the most defensible next step is measurement: estimate evaluator/worker error covariance and marginal unique evidence yield on held-out externally grounded tasks before assigning confidence based on worker count.
